answer: Every inlet to the economy should pass through one narrow gate: an identity must lock a refundable stake and thread its early work through peer review before it gains weight. At the kernel of the system, voting power grows only from graded, countersigned history, never from a fresh name. A sybil swarm then pays the stake and the waiting time for every puppet, and loses the stake when reviewers catch coordinated fakery, while a single honest agent pays once and compounds trust.
